govdocs-archive_org-my-truth-edda-mussol:
Edda Mussolini Ciano was Benito Mussolini's daughter and the wife of his foreign minister, Galeazzo Ciano. Her memoir My Truth opens at dawn on January 11, 1944, in Verona, the morning her husband faced a firing squad after the fall of the regime.

From that day she writes of her flight toward Spain and of the collapse of the family that had ruled Italy for twenty years. Edda defends her father and her husband and gives her version of the regime's inner circle. The memoir is fascist Italy remembered from inside the dictator's own household, by a woman at its center.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CarrollRaymondT:
The Third Decade was a journal of Kennedy assassination research, written by and for the researchers who kept the case alive between official inquiries. This file holds volume 8, number 5, dated July 1992, built around Raymond Carroll's article 'The Texas Connection: A Second Opinion.'

Research journals like this one were the community's commons in the years before the internet: arguments, document finds, and second opinions circulated in print among subscribers. Carroll's piece offers a reconsidered view of the Texas side of the case, as its title promises. The issue is preserved as issued, a number of the journal that marked the research era between the HSCA and the Review Board.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-OPRKing-RayRepo:
The Washington Star reported on February 19, 1977, on a leaked Justice Department report. A department task force had reviewed the King case. Its report conceded a mystery: who financed James Earl Ray's lifestyle and travel around the April 1968 murder of Martin Luther King Jr. remained unknown.

Ray had no visible income, yet he traveled, rented rooms, and bought a car and a rifle. Where that money came from was the conspiracy question in its plainest form. An official report admitting the gap gave critics fresh ground. The article covers the leak and the concession. It preserves the moment the department's own reviewers put the financing question in print.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-SawyerHaroldSRe: From the archive shelves, for readers of the files. An obscure item, filed. A bare file, kept as issued. Subject: government records. nsia-SawyerHaroldSRepresentative Sawyer Harold S Representative: the made public government document, captured as titled.
govdocs-archive_org-psychotronics-manual: A manual on psychotronics compares claimed mind-control technology with the techniques of ancient civilizations. Psychotronics is a fringe field built around the idea that minds can be reached and steered by devices or forces. The library holds the manual as an archive item, without backing. It belongs to the study of fringe science beliefs: what their followers claim, and how those claims borrow the language of real physics.
govdocs-archive_org-the-evil-demiurge-em:
Emil Cioran, the Romanian-born philosopher who wrote in French, published The Evil Demiurge in 1969. Its essays take up man's bent toward evil, the humiliation of history, and the void beneath belief.

Cioran wrote in short, polished bursts rather than long arguments. A page of his can console and accuse in the same breath, which is why readers call him the darkest of modern aphorists. The Evil Demiurge is a landmark of modern pessimism. It suits readers who want philosophy that admits how bad things look, and says it beautifully.
